title: Velocity Global Competitors: 8 Alternatives for Global Hiring
summary: Exploring Velocity Global competitors? Ontop breaks down 8 real alternatives to help you hire globally at lower cost and with less complexity.
body_text: Expanding a team across borders comes with real complexity: payroll compliance, contractor classification, local tax laws, and currency management all require attention at once. Choosing the wrong platform can cost a business significant time and money, which is why understanding the landscape of Velocity Global competitors and alternatives matters before committing to a solution. ‍ Not every global employment platform is built the same way. Some lean heavily on employer-of-record services, while others offer leaner, more flexible options for managing cross-border payments and workforce compliance. Companies hiring international contractors or remote teams can explore a purpose-built payroll software like Ontop to see how it stacks up against the alternatives. According to Velocity Global data cited by Forbes, 62% of employees would take a 10% pay cut to remain remote, which means the tools managing their employment are no longer administrative back-office decisions. They are part of the value proposition workers are actively protecting. The traditional Employer of Record model was designed for a specific legal problem: how to hire a full-time employee in a country where a company has no legal entity. That structure carries real costs, starting at $599 per employee per month with some providers, and it adds compliance layers that simply do not match the needs of companies whose international workforce is primarily contractors rather than full-time employees. Country coverage numbers are often misleading when evaluating global employment platforms. A provider claiming support in 185+ countries may still require weeks of setup in the specific markets where a company actually hires. The number that matters is how well a platform performs in the hiring markets a company uses most, not the total count on a feature matrix. Worker experience has measurable financial consequences that most platform evaluations ignore. Companies that invest in employee experience are 4x more profitable than those that do not, according to HappySignals' 2025 research, and companies with highly engaged employees outperform peers by 147% in earnings per share. Platforms designed primarily for HR administrators rather than for the contractors using them create friction that quietly compounds into a retention problem. Payment reliability is no longer a differentiator for global contractors. It is a baseline expectation. With 98% of remote workers reporting they want to continue working remotely for the rest of their careers (Neat's State of Remote Work 2025), professionals are making long-term decisions about which employment arrangements to stay in, and slow or opaque payment experiences directly influence those decisions. Background screening accuracy remains the top priority among global hiring professionals, according to HireRight's 2025 Global Benchmark Report. Platforms that rush onboarding without reliable verification create legal exposure, while those that prioritize accuracy through manual workflows slow hiring to a crawl. The right platform holds both without trading one for the other. Payroll software built around contractor-first infrastructure addresses these gaps by giving workers direct access to contracts, payment records, and account management without adding administrative overhead for employers. Why Companies and Remote Workers Look for Velocity Global Competitors Velocity Global solved a real problem: hiring someone in another country without having to set up a legal entity there. But global hiring has matured . According to Hire Borderless , 74% of companies plan to hire internationally in the next 12 months — global talent acquisition is now a baseline expectation , not a strategic edge . When that many organizations hire across borders, the market breaks into different segments . Different companies have different needs, budgets , and definitions of what "working well" actually means. ‍ " 74% of companies plan to hire internationally in the next 12 months —global talent acquisition is now a baseline expectation , not a strategic edge." — Hire Borderless ‍ 🔑 Takeaway: When nearly 3 in 4 companies are hiring across borders, the question is no longer whether to go global—it's which platform fits your specific needs, budget, and scale. ‍ 💡 Why This Matters: The EOR market has expanded far beyond a one-size-fits-all solution. Companies now segment by cost sensitivity , compliance complexity , contractor vs. employee needs , and regional focus —making it essential to evaluate Velocity Global alternatives against your actual requirements. ‍ Segment Startups & SMBs Primary Need Affordable global hiring Key Decision Factor Cost and simplicity Segment Mid-market companies Primary Need Scalable compliance Key Decision Factor Coverage and speed Segment Enterprise organizations Primary Need Full-service EOR + integrations Key Decision Factor Reliability and support Segment Contractor-heavy teams Primary Need Flexible, non-employee hiring Key Decision Factor Contractor management tools ‍ Gateway scene representing access to global hiring markets Where does the EOR model start to break down? The failure point is usually structural overhead. Most EOR platforms were designed around a single model: the provider becomes the employer of record, assumes compliance risk, and charges accordingly. That works for full-time employees in countries where you have no entity, but it becomes expensive and creates friction when you need to pay a skilled contractor in Colombia or Nigeria quickly and compliantly, without months-long onboarding. The architecture stops matching the problem. ‍ Most companies layer workarounds on top of their existing provider: contractor payment tools, separate compliance checks, and manual currency-specific payment runs. As teams expand globally, these workarounds multiply. Payroll software built for contractor-first global teams moves from setup to first payment in minutes across 150+ countries, while our platform gives contractors a global account to receive, spend, and manage earnings, rather than routing payments through legacy banking systems. How does platform friction affect remote worker retention? Remote workers feel this friction directly. According to Velocity Global, cited by Forbes , 62% of employees would take a 10% pay cut to stay remote. Remote work is now a financial and lifestyle choice that people actively protect. When the platform managing their payments is slow, unclear, or hard to use, workers notice. In a competitive talent market, that experience affects whether workers stay. ‍ Comparing Velocity Global competitors is not about finding a cheaper alternative. It is about recognizing that the EOR model , built for a different era of global work, carries structural costs many companies no longer need. Organizations making this comparison have outgrown the assumptions embedded in the original solution. Which platform category best fits your workforce? Was the platform designed for the workforce you actually have? No platform is universally right. The choice depends on your workforce composition , growth trajectory, and what global hiring should feel like for your workers. The key question is: was the platform designed for your current workforce or for one from a decade ago? ‍ Once you understand what the platform delivers to your business, a separate question most evaluations never ask remains. Just Say the Word: A More Personal Way to Ask, Discover, and Listen
summary: Spotify has always been built around your taste. Now, we’re making it easier to shape what you hear, understand what’s playing, and explore your listening—just by asking. Eligible Premium users will see new ways to talk to Spotify across Home and the Now Playing view on mobile. By typing or speaking directly in the app,...
body_text: Spotify has always been built around your taste. Now, we’re making it easier to shape what you hear, understand what’s playing, and explore your listening—just by asking. Eligible Premium users will see new ways to talk to Spotify across Home and the Now Playing view on mobile. By typing or speaking directly in the app, you can have a back-and-forth conversation to choose what’s playing, learn about the music you love, revisit your listening history, and go deeper on podcasts and audiobooks, all without leaving Spotify. https://storage.googleapis.com/pr-newsroom-wp/1/2026/07/You-can-now-talk-to-Spotify_demo-smaller-37492387492734.mp4 Soundtrack any moment Some days you know exactly what you want to hear. Other times, you want to change it up as you go. Ask Spotify to “Play some artists I haven’t heard before,” then keep shaping the vibe with as much or as little direction as you want. You can say, “Add some Bad Bunny ,” and then ask to narrow it to “just his recent stuff,” or “make it more upbeat.” And when you love what you hear, ask Spotify to “save this song,” “add this to my queue,” or “follow this artist.” Understand what’s playing Want to learn more about your favorite song, album, artist, or genre? Ask from the Now Playing view. Try “What is the inspiration behind Dua Lipa ’s Radical Optimism ?” “When was this album released?” or “What genre is this?” Spotify can give you more context, then guide you to related artists, sounds, and stories that deepen your discovery of music and the creative processes behind it. The experience goes beyond music. While listening to a podcast or audiobook, you can ask about the people, stories, and ideas behind it from “What other books has this author written?” to “What other podcasts has this guest been on?” Explore your listening Because Spotify understands your playlists, favorite artists, repeat listens, and listening history, it can help answer questions about your taste. Ask “When did I first listen to this song?” or “What genres have I been into recently?” It’s a new way to explore the story of your taste, from the songs you keep on repeat to the artists, genres, and moments that shaped it. A more personal way to listen The new conversational experience is part of our ongoing work to make Spotify more personal and useful for every listener, giving people more ways to get the most out of every moment. Use it your way: press the mic button to talk, type instead, or keep listening like you always have. It’s rolling out gradually in beta for Premium users 18+ in the U.S., Ireland, and Sweden across iOS and Android devices in English. Like any beta, it’s a work in progress: responses won’t always be perfect, and your feedback directly shapes what comes next. Stay tuned for more updates as we build new ways to connect listeners with the music, podcasts, audiobooks, artists, and creators they love.

title: Multiply Labs Establishes Italian Manufacturing Subsidiary, Names Former Scuderia Ferrari (F1) Leader as Founding General Manager
body_text: SAN FRANCISCO and TURIN, ITALY — MAY 27, 2026 — Multiply Labs, the company spearheading physical AI for biomanufacturing, has announced the launch of Multiply Labs Italia , the company's first international subsidiary, and the appointment of Enrico Antonio Racca as founding General Manager. Racca, who most recently served as Head of Supply Chain and Manufacturing for Scuderia Ferrari, joins Multiply Labs to scale production of the company's robotic clusters that manufacture advanced therapies at industrial scale. He also assumes the role of Chief of Supply Chain and Manufacturing for Multiply Labs Inc., the U.S. parent. Multiply Labs Italia is being established in Turin to build the manufacturing capacity required to deliver Multiply Labs' robotic clusters to a growing roster of pharmaceutical customers, including AstraZeneca, Legend Biotech, and Kyverna Therapeutics. The Italian entity is being built from the ground up, with responsibility for recruiting and developing the manufacturing team, designing the supply chain for large-scale cluster production, and establishing the quality systems required for regulated pharmaceutical environments. Racca brings to the role more than two decades of high-performance manufacturing leadership. As Head of Supply Chain and Manufacturing for Scuderia Ferrari from 2021 to 2025, he led a 650-person organization, reporting directly to the Team Principal. Before joining Scuderia Ferrari in 2015, Enrico spent more than a decade at Fiat Group and Fiat-Chrysler Group, including four years as Global Commodity Manager overseeing a €4 billion global procurement portfolio across drive systems, chassis, exhaust, and shifters. “We believe that bringing world-class manufacturing discipline to physical AI and biotech is the only way to deliver advanced therapies to every patient who needs them. Enrico has spent his career scaling some of the most demanding electromechanical manufacturing operations in the world. His leadership will be transformative for our growth, and as we establish Multiply Labs Italia and scale our production capacity globally.” Fred Parietti, PhD, Co-Founder & CEO, Multiply Labs Enrico Racca (left) and Fred Parietti (right) in front of a Multiply Labs prototype cluster. “Manufacturing advanced therapies requires the same precision and discipline that defines Formula 1. I am proud to be establishing Multiply Labs Italia and joining the leadership team to scale Multiply Labs’ robotic clusters to pharmaceutical customers worldwide.” Enrico Antonio Racca, Founding General Manager, Multiply Labs Italia He holds a master’s degree in Electrical Engineering from Politecnico di Torino, where he graduated in the top 2% of his class, and an MBA from Università degli Studi di Torino. Multiply Labs is bringing Physical AI to life sciences: the first autonomous manufacturing platform for biologics, starting with cell therapy, the most complex manufacturing challenge in medicine. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, Multiply Labs is led by co-founders Fred Parietti and Alice Melocchi.

title: Do you really know how your customers will behave?
summary: As technology changes, so do customer behaviors, and so must our business processes. (I use the term customer loosely here to represent the larger set of consumers, employees, citizens and other stakeholders that may be among your target audiences.)
body_text: As technology changes, so do customer behaviors, and so must our business processes. (I use the term customer loosely here to represent the larger set of consumers, employees, citizens and other stakeholders that may be among your target audiences.) When the majority of your customers have decided that digital is their preferred way to interact with your organization, the tipping point for digital transformation has been reached. At this point, there is a need to exploit your readily accessible data to better understand how your customers are behaving so you can continuously evaluate and improve your strategies, processes and communications. Data on your customers’ past behavior can help you make accurate predictions about their future behavior, allowing you to not just anticipate, but influence, their behavior to drive profits, increase efficiency, improve service and better manage risk. Go with the facts, not your gut A common temptation is to try to project oneself into the customer’s shoes by asking questions like, “If I were to receive the communication I just designed, how would I react?” While this method may feel rational, the evidence is quite overwhelming that such approaches are highly prone to bias and error. The plain fact is we cannot safely rely upon our own personal instincts to predict how our customers are likely to respond to a marketing offer, a reminder, a warning or a particular situation. So we need to look at what is actually happening in practice and understand what our customers are telling us from their true actions and behaviors. Here’s an excellent example of this point. Traditional approaches to government debt collection have assumed that the more information debtors receive, the more likely they are to pay (if able), and that clear explanations should be sufficient to prompt debtors to behave rationally. In fact, however, the unconscious system has been found to be much more influential than previously thought. As a result, when it comes to something as highly emotional as parting with one’s own money, it can no longer be assumed that supplying facts and rational arguments alone will persuade people to resolve their liabilities. Instead, collection strategies must be designed much more carefully to reflect how people respond based on real-life rather than theory. I invite you to read our white paper on using behavioral science in government debt collection to improve outcomes, increase revenue collected and reduce non-compliance for more information. While executive intuition and instinct will continue to have their place in corporate and operational decision-making, we believe organizations large and small can deliver bottom-line benefits by tapping the enormous value contained in their own customer data, and enabling the facts and evidence to have a much bigger say in their decision-making.
